_comment: ROT: what a thing becomes past its end. WORLD.md, locked: 'Age a thing forward past
its end: compost, spoil, collapse. NEVER AIMED AT A PLAYER OR A MOB.'
THIS IS THE AGEING TABLE CONTINUED. The Turning's chains stop at mossy cobblestone,
mossy stone bricks and cobbled deepslate -- terminal states, things with no next
step. Rot gives them one. `stone -> cobblestone -> mossy cobblestone` is what a wall
does over a long time; the row below is what it does after that, and it is the same
sentence finished rather than a second idea.
SEPARATE FROM THE AGEING TABLE, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN. Rewind reads the Turning's
table backwards, so anything in it can be undone -- which is what 'keeping every
past' means when it is a block. Nothing here is in that table, so nothing here can
be rewound. Past a thing's end there is no past left to keep, and the god that
remembers everything remembers everything a thing WAS, not what is left of it.
NOTHING HERE IS A CREATURE, and it is not a creature by construction rather than by
a rule: this is a block-conversion table and a table of blocks has no way to name a
cow. WORLD.md rules out the obvious reading of 'age it past its end' -- an
instant-kill -- because EVERY SPELL IS A WORLD-VERB, and a school that broke the
doctrine would take the doctrine with it.
THREE RULES END AT GRAVEL, which the table permits and records: asking what a piece
of gravel used to be has three answers and no way to choose. See StepTable -- a
converging `to` is refused for reading backwards rather than forbidden, and here it
is the honest shape. A collapsed wall does not remember which wall it was.
